relations.why: A token-shaped literal assigned to the Auth.js secret is reported by both rules.
relations.settle: Keep both: AUTH-SECRET-001 also catches secrets that do not look like a known token. Reading the secret from the environment satisfies both.

source.paraphrase: Source does not contain real API keys, tokens, private keys or credentialed connection strings. Exact known URL-password placeholders in test fixtures are distinguished from real credentials.

invariants.why: A secret in source is copied into git, into logs, and into every worktree. Rotation then means rewriting history.
invariants.fixHint: Read the value from the environment or a secret manager. Commit a name, not the value.
invariants.avoid: A short sk_live_test is below the token threshold. Only a complete static URL literal with password secret, password or changeme is exempt in a .test/.spec file; comments, production URLs, interpolated URLs and real-looking credentials still match. Splitting a real token across expressions hides it and does not remove the secret.

source.paraphrase: A public env prefix must not wrap a server secret. The value would be readable from shipped client code.

invariants.why: Those prefixes are inlined into the client bundle. A server secret under that name ships to the browser.
invariants.fixHint: Keep the secret in an unprefixed server env var. Expose only values that are safe to publish, such as a public API URL.
invariants.avoid: Renaming the suffix to KEY still matches when the name contains SECRET or TOKEN. A server-only STRIPE_SECRET without the public prefix is not this rule.
